criteria.local_only_remodel: Hold the line: imported parents stay illegal, and each of the 20 sites is rewritten by its draft owner into reference-plus-invariant form with re-proven policy, default and composition parity at every seam. Nothing cross-package is ever promised because nothing cross-package exists. This demands the most human effort, repeats the levy on every future imported-containment need, strains the rule against blanket rewrites, and spends it all to defend a checker restriction rather than an established semantic requirement, while the drafts plainly prefer canonical parents.
criteria.owner_consent_facet: Let each owner decide: imported containment compiles only under a parent the owning package explicitly marks containable, conferring the full local relation under marked parents and a marker-directed rejection elsewhere, with bound parents excluded either way. Open design debt includes the marking syntax, its visibility and versioning semantics, default reverse-collection exposure, and optional depth and cascade bounds. Three one-line owner edits plus a new language feature, consumers paced by owner shipments, and a mechanism whose protection is vacuous among same-project packages and whose atomicity assurances stop exactly where remote parents begin.
criteria.plain_import_containment: Extend the existing local relation across plain imports untouched: same immutable parent reference, same inherited team and storage ownership, same atomic subtree archive, same parent-scoped uniqueness, same typed child collections with policy-gated readability, same cycle rejection now computed over the whole-app index. Zero edits at the 20 draft sites. Bound parents are refused with a diagnostic. Accepted exposures: consumer-triggered cascades reaching owner-adjacent rows, uniqueness constraints spanning the package edge, cross-boundary diagnostics to author, index-wide engine work to finish, and a future deployment split that could strand the atomicity guarantee without any firing alarm; the engine proof is explicitly still owed.
criteria.reference_scoping: Split form from lifecycle: the child still names its imported parent through a required immutable link with inherited team and storage and parent-scoped uniqueness, but parent archive and delete stop at the package edge and reverse navigation is computed on demand. Lifecycle authority never crosses packages, so atomicity across the edge is never owed. The levy is conceptual: two behaviors behind one keyword, an invented orphan disposition (forbid the archive or detach the children) with no grounding in the 20 read sites, perpetual vigilance in every later `in` feature to keep the meanings apart, and hand-rolled cascade wherever any workflow eventually requires it.

containment_rule.instructions: Considering authoring effort, review burden, future maintenance and fidelity to the drafts' stated relational intent, which rule resolves the 20 imported-containment sites most economically without breaking accepted workflows or weakening negatives? Apply identical workflow and minimal-intervention standards to all four.

request.state: The CanLang audit faces 20 child-in-imported-parent declarations spread over six accepted workflows in a 52-file draft corpus. Employee is the stated parent for Expense, Leave and Onboard children; Customer for Invoice, Propose and Service children; Location for Reception children. Import analysis is unanimous: each parent is plainly imported, and a corpus-wide survey of 76 bound from= import lines shows none of them parenting any containment, so remote-parent containment is unexercised speculation. Nested three-deep relations with parent.parent defaults and row.parent.* policy reads are part of the accepted set. A full read of all 20 sites plus the three owner packages finds no statement of delete or archive expectations for imported children, with four near-miss passages that fail to decide. Design text assigns included imports to the owner's store under a single atomic commit, but the implemented engine performs no cross-package subtree expansion, generated operations commit via a provisional route, and the specified split behavior (fail before commit, no cross-store transaction) emits no diagnostic. No containment-endorsement construct exists; owner attitudes are unobservable in source. Whatever is chosen must keep containment cycles erroneous, preserve wrong/cross-team/missing-parent failures, grant parents no mutation powers to importers, and confront each contender's gravest flaw: deployment-split exposure, keyword double meaning, whole-corpus remodeling, or owner-paced consent lacking atomicity payoff. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
